resources.string: Chain
Combine Aether, Psiphon, and Tor. More hops can bypass more filters, but reduce speed.
Cores
Path: %1$s
Aether
Aether alone;the fastest option. Start here; add hops only if it cannot connect.
Psiphon
Psiphon alone. Try it when your network blocks Cloudflare WARP.
Tor
Tor alone. Slow and blocked on many networks in Iran. Does not guarantee anonymity.
Psiphon over Aether
Psiphon connects through Aether. Your operator sees WARP traffic instead of Psiphon.
Tor over Aether
Tor connects through Aether, which may help conceal Tor use. Use it when Tor cannot connect.
Tor over Psiphon
Tor connects through Psiphon. Use it when both Tor and WARP are blocked.
Tor over Psiphon over Aether
All three stacked: the slowest option and a last resort.
Psiphon is ready. No setup is required.
This build has no Psiphon server list, so Psiphon cannot start. Run scripts/fetch-psiphon-serverlist.sh and rebuild.
Psiphon exit country
Automatic (fastest server)
This is where traffic exits. Keep Automatic unless you need a country; Psiphon chooses the fastest reachable server.
If no server is available in your chosen country, Psiphon connects elsewhere.
Tor adds three relays: expect much higher latency, and no UDP at all, so video calls and QUIC fall back to TCP or stop working. The first connection can take a few minutes.
Tor exit country
e.g. de
Two-letter country code for the exit relay. Needs the geoip database bundled in the build; leave empty to let Tor choose.
Only that country
Never fall back to another country when the one you chose has no usable exit. That can mean no connection at all.
